text:
Alex G: flagging an uptick in p95/p99 on /v1/generate starting ~08:27 UTC. p50 unchanged. customers reporting sluggishness. can runtime/SRE pair investigate?

Maria V: which customers and which model variants? can you paste the dashboard snippets and any traces?

Alex G: seeing it for acct-42 and acct-77 and our test-customer integration. quick metrics snapshot: p50 ~130ms, p95 jumped from ~900ms to 2.1s, p99 from ~1.5s to ~4.2s. error rate small but timeouts present.

Cheng H: I just looked at cache telemetry: prefix/kv cache miss rate spiked sharply at 08:25-08:28 on nodepool-runtime-3. eviction churn also elevated. posting the query I used: 
```
100 * (sum by(node) (increase(runtime_kv_cache_misses_total[3m])) / sum by(node) (increase(runtime_kv_cache_requests_total[3m])))
```
went from ~1-3% to ~40% on that pool.

Dev Support: any deploys around that window? need a sample request that shows the problematic prefix key pattern to reproduce.

Alex G: there was a small canary (runtime v3.14) started at 08:10. example request I captured (redacted):
```
{
  "prompt": "Explain...",
  "prefix_key": "acct-77:session:abcd:ts-2026-03-15T08:26:31Z",
  "max_tokens": 250
}
```

Cheng H: that prefix_key format is likely the culprit. appending exact timestamps makes cache keys high-cardinality. each request looks unique -> misses -> heavy compute. also seen in stack traces: hot functions `prepare_kv_cache_key` and `kv_get_or_populate`.

Maria V: current per-shard cache is LRU with ~48 shards and small capacity; LRU suffers when keys are transient. suggestions: temporarily increase total prefix cache size and switch those shards to TTL-based eviction to reduce thrash. also we should normalize keys server-side to strip high-entropy suffixes.

Sam R: checking backend store (redis) metrics now redis throughput looks normal, no command latencies. confirms issue is front-end cache churn not backend saturation. can we get a flamegraph and pprof of runtime process?

Alex G: reproduction steps I ran: 1) send 200 concurrent requests changing only the suffix timestamp in prefix_key -> miss rate ~45% and p95 high; 2) repeat with fixed prefix key -> miss rate ~2% and p95 normal.

Dev Support: mitigation choices?

Cheng H: immediate: reduce canary weight or rollback if it's >5% traffic. medium: bump cache sizes on affected pool and change eviction to TTL(10m) for prefix caches. long: implement key normalization and add guardrails in SDK/docs to discourage timestamped keys. also add telemetry for unique-prefix cardinality per minute with alerting.

Alex G: I rolled the canary back at 08:40 and observed a gradual p95 decline but misses stayed elevated until caches warmed.

Cheng H: applied temporary config at 08:47 to nodepool-runtime-3:
```
runtime.kv.prefix_cache_total_mb = 2300  # increased from 1600
runtime.kv.prefix_cache_shards = 64
runtime.kv.prefix_cache_eviction = ttl
runtime.kv.prefix_cache_ttl_seconds = 600
```
Warmup took ~10 minutes. after warmup (09:05) p95 ~160ms, p99 ~420ms, kv_miss_rate ~3.4%.

Maria V: follow-ups to track: 1) code change to normalize prefix keys + enforce a max key length and a whitelist for acceptable patterns; 2) expose cardinality metric and alert when unique-prefixes/min > threshold; 3) update SDK examples and docs to call out anti-patterns (don\u2019t embed per-request timestamps).

Sam R: I'll open the runtime PR to add normalization behind a config flag (opt-out) and unit tests. also adding a prewarm API endpoint to allow customers to register canonical prefix keys before traffic ramps.

Dev Support: customer outreach plan: tell acct-42 and acct-77 we traced it to high-cardinality prefix keys causing cache thrash, we rolled back canary and increased cache to mitigate, permanent fix in review and SDK guidance forthcoming. offer to help them migrate keys. cc: solutions and account teams.

Alex G: final post-mitigation metrics at 09:22: p50 115ms, p95 150ms, p99 420ms, kv_miss_rate ~3.2%. SRE Bot cleared the alert at 09:26.

SRE Bot: alert resolved: high_kv_cache_miss_rate on nodepool-runtime-3 at 09:26:02 UTC :white_check_mark:

Cheng H: created follow-up backlog tickets: CACHE-298 (prefix-key-normalization), CACHE-302 (prefix-cardinality-telemetry), CACHE-305 (prewarm-api). will triage priorities with product this week.

Maria V: also patch notes for next release and a short runbook for customer-facing engineers explaining how to identify prefix-key thrash and recommended mitigations.

Alex G: thanks all for the quick turnaround. I'll attach traces and sample logs in a linked thread and follow up with customer comms.
